attributes.description: Every event judged flagged by either sensor, newest first, with its indicators. Share > CSV in Discover exports it as an IOC feed.
attributes.title: Threat Intel: Flagged Event Feed

attributes.description: Planted honeytokens being reused and hijacked sessions: proof a user took something from the honeypot and tried to use it.
attributes.title: Threat Intel: Credential & Session Abuse

attributes.description: Docker, Redis and nginx-error log lines newest first -- the raw operational feed behind the Infrastructure panels, for spotting a crash loop or an error burst. Share > CSV in Discover exports it.
attributes.title: Infrastructure: Recent Log Lines

attributes.description: Individual metric samples as Vector's metric_to_log flattens them: the series `name`, whether it is a cumulative `counter.value` or point-in-time `gauge.value`, and which Vector process (`vector_role`) or host emitted it. The ground truth behind the Pipeline & Host Health panels -- and the quickest way to see the exact metric names Vector is shipping.
attributes.title: Pipeline & Host: Raw Metric Samples

attributes.description: Every pool lifecycle event newest first -- builds (with per-phase timings), hand-offs (how long a session waited), health checks, scaledowns and cap/uncap decisions. The raw log behind the Pool & Capacity latency panels; Share > CSV in Discover exports it.
attributes.title: Pool: Lifecycle Event Feed

attributes.description: Every detection pattern the honeypot currently has enabled, with its category, severity, where it fires and how many Suricata SIDs it carries -- the full coverage list behind the Detection Coverage panels. Drop the enabled:true filter in Discover to see disabled patterns too; Share > CSV exports it.
attributes.title: Detection: Enabled Pattern List

attributes.description: Network IDS view: alert severity over time, categories, protocols, targeted ports, top signatures and source IPs.
attributes.title: Honeypot: IDS Alerts (Suricata)

attributes.description: What was requested and how it was answered: volume by route, status codes, methods, top URIs marked attack_pattern or safe, and which static assets were served from cache.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Web Traffic & Threat Overview

attributes.description: Why each request was routed where it was: own vs. carried-over score against the honeypot threshold, decay states, offenses and routing reasons.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Threat Decisions & Decay

attributes.description: Per-session request volume and duration, peak threat, offenses and user-sophistication classification.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Session Analysis

attributes.description: Which attack patterns and CVEs requests matched, the URIs behind them, honeytoken hits and top attacking IPs.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Attack Patterns

attributes.description: User indicators across the proxy and Suricata: IOC list per IP, MITRE ATT&CK techniques and kill-chain stage reached, attack tools, CVEs targeted, and an exportable flagged-event feed.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Threat Intelligence

attributes.description: Operational health of the stack itself: container log volume by service and stream, nginx error/info levels over time, Redis session-store activity, and a raw infrastructure log feed.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Infrastructure & Ops Logs

attributes.description: The observability pipeline's own health and the edge host's resources: Vector throughput, buffer fill and errors for both shippers, plus host CPU load, memory, network and disk.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Pipeline & Host Health

attributes.description: The honeypot pool fleet's live state and how fast it scales: ready/free/waiting/building pools over time, state mix, per-session hand-off waits and per-pool build latency, plus the edge host's load and memory as the manager sees them.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Pool & Capacity

attributes.description: Which attack patterns the honeypot currently has enabled: the Lua/Suricata detection the dashboard's Pattern Database has switched on, snapshotted into the SIEM -- enabled vs disabled, by category, severity and kind, which were toggled from the default, and the full enabled-pattern list.
attributes.title: Honeypot: Detection Coverage
